title: Sampling: head, tail, and keeping the trace that mattered

videos.script: So far the lab has kept every trace. At five checkouts a second that is already forty spans a second, and a real shop is a hundred times busier. {{cost}} Sampling means keeping some traces and dropping the rest. The whole lesson is about which ones, and who decides. {{choice}} You decide first at the front door, before anything has happened. That is cheap, and it is blind. It drops the slow checkout as readily as the fast one. {{head}} Then you let one service ignore that decision, and watch the traces break in half. {{broken}} Then the Collector decides at the end, once each trace is complete. It keeps every error, every slow request, and a few of the rest. {{tail}} And you keep the counts honest. The rates and the latencies are computed from every span, before any of them is dropped. {{metrics}}
